implementation_notes: Go has the tightest instrument of any language here: the compiler rejects unused imports and unused local variables outright, so those categories of anchor cannot exist. What remains is unused *packages* listed in `go.mod` (Go deliberately does not prune them), unused exported identifiers, unused struct fields, and unused methods — none of which the compiler reports. `go mod tidy` handles the first mechanically and is the single highest-value command for this smell; `staticcheck`'s U1000 (unused code) family and `unused` from honnef.co handle the rest, with the usual caveat that anything reachable only through `interface{}`, reflection or `init()` will be reported as unused incorrectly.
idiom_name: unused package in go.mod; unused exported identifier
pitfalls: `go mod tidy` cannot remove a dependency that a `//go:build tools` import or a code generator keeps alive.
`init()` functions run whether or not anything references them, so their contents are anchors the unused-detector may misjudge.
Interface satisfaction is implicit, so a method may be dead in the compiler's view and live through an interface — treat `unused` output as a prompt, not a verdict.
